title: Eager Multi-Aggregate Serialization (The Over-fetched JSON DTO)
damaged_code:
```rust
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct CustomerDto {
    id: u64,
    name: String,
    orders: Vec<OrderDto>,           // Nested separate aggregate
    billing_info: BillingInfoDto,     // Nested separate aggregate
}
```
pattern: Serialization structures (DTOs) that transitively bundle entire clusters of unrelated Aggregates in a single deep hierarchy.
why_bad: It causes massive database over-fetching, heavy serialization latency, and bloated memory allocations (referred to as "jigsaw puzzle pieces in many dimensions"). It also breaches transactional boundary rules by mixing independent transactional units.
detection: Match structs decorated with `#[derive(Serialize)]` containing nested lists or child structs that represent distinct aggregate roots.
counterexample:
An aggregate root nesting its own local constituent value objects that cannot exist independently:
```rust
struct OrderDto {
    id: u64,
    items: Vec<OrderItemDto>, // Local value objects
}
```
fix:
Use identity pointers (e.g., `customer_id: u64`) to relate aggregates, or create specialized, flattened DTOs optimized for specific UI screens.
```rust
struct CustomerDto {
    id: u64,
    name: String,
    order_ids: Vec<u64>,
}
```
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (Chapter 10, "Clustering Entities and Value Objects", p. 348; Chapter 14, p. 513).
